name: Colorado Artificial Intelligence Act (SB 24-205)
description: Colorado SB 24-205 (Consumer Protections for Artificial Intelligence Act) overlay. Effective June 30, 2026 (delayed from February 1, 2026 by SB 25B-004). First comprehensive US state AI governance law. Applies to 'deployers' that use high-risk AI systems to make consequential decisions affecting Colorado consumers in education, employment, financial services, health care, housing, insurance, and legal services. Key obligations: risk management policy, impact assessment before deployment, annual review, consumer notices, appeal mechanism. Safe harbor: compliance with a recognized AI risk management framework (ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, or AG-designated equivalent) provides affirmative defense to algorithmic discrimination claims. Enforcement: Colorado AG exclusive; no private right of action; 60-day cure period; up to $2,000/violation.

evidence_requirements: Written risk management policy for each high-risk AI system documented and approved (CRS §6-1-1702(2)(a))
Risk management policy aligned with a recognized framework (ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, or Colorado AG-designated equivalent) to support affirmative defense
Policy covers: AI system purpose, risk identification process, mitigation measures, monitoring plan, and accountability structure
Developer documentation received and retained — model cards, dataset cards, or equivalent technical documentation provided by AI system developers (CRS §6-1-1702(3)(a))
GOV-01.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702(2)(a) — Deployer risk management policy obligation

evidence_requirements: Named responsible individual or team for each high-risk AI system documented
Accountability chain for consequential AI decisions documented — deployer responsibility acknowledged
Developer-deployer relationship documented where applicable — records of developer documentation received per CRS §6-1-1702(3)(a)
Contact information for consumer AI inquiries designated and accessible (required in pre-decision consumer notice)
GOV-02.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702 — Developer and deployer accountability obligations

evidence_requirements: Risk tolerance for each high-risk AI system defined and documented as part of risk management policy

Impact assessment conducted before deployment — must address: purpose, benefits, foreseeable risks, algorithmic discrimination risk, mitigation measures, post-deployment monitoring plan (CRS §6-1-1702(2)(b))
Risk acceptance rationale documented for residual risks following mitigation
Algorithmic discrimination risk specifically assessed — analysis of whether AI system could cause unfair or discriminatory outcomes in the covered consequential decision domain
Human oversight configuration documented — level of human review for consequential AI decisions
Pre-decision consumer notice documented and implemented: notice to consumer that a high-risk AI system is used, type of system, and contact information for inquiries (CRS §6-1-1702(2)(c)(I))
Consumer notice delivered BEFORE the high-risk AI system makes the consequential decision
Website disclosure published listing all high-risk AI systems deployed, their purposes, and types of consequential decisions made (CRS §6-1-1702(2)(e))
Note: Colorado consumer notice obligations go beyond AKSI's oversight configuration scope. Evidence must include actual notice delivery records, not just configuration documentation.
GOV-04.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702(2)(c)(I) and §6-1-1702(2)(e) — Consumer notice and website disclosure obligations

evidence_requirements: Inventory of all high-risk AI systems deployed — includes: system name/description, consequential decision domain, deployment date, accountable owner
Inventory used as basis for website disclosure required under CRS §6-1-1702(2)(e)
Inventory updated when new high-risk AI systems are deployed or existing systems materially changed
Consumer-accessible disclosure version maintained at public-facing URL
ID-01.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702(2)(e) — Website disclosure obligation (requires enumeration of deployed high-risk AI systems)

evidence_requirements: Third-party AI tools and model providers used in high-risk AI systems documented
Developer documentation received and retained — model cards, dataset documentation, known risks disclosed by developer
Note: Colorado places documentation obligations on developers to provide documentation to deployers. Deployer evidence requirement includes records of developer documentation received.
Data inputs to high-risk AI systems documented — personal data types, sources, and classification
Training data documentation received from developer — dataset cards, bias assessments, known limitations
Personal data used in consequential decisions identified — supports consumer data correction right under CRS §6-1-1702(2)(c)(II)
Data accuracy controls documented — process for identifying and correcting inaccurate personal data used in AI decisions
ID-03.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702(2)(b) and §6-1-1702(2)(c)(II) — Impact assessment data documentation + consumer data correction

evidence_requirements: Third-party AI system providers assessed — developer-furnished documentation reviewed as part of deployer due diligence
Developer risk disclosures received and documented — any developer-disclosed known or foreseeable risks of algorithmic discrimination

Note: Colorado creates a developer-to-deployer documentation handoff obligation. Deployer evidence should include records of documentation received from each AI developer, confirming the supply chain governance chain.
ID-04.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702(3)(a) — Developer documentation obligations; deployer due diligence

evidence_requirements: Impact assessment completed before deployment of each high-risk AI system (CRS §6-1-1702(2)(b))
Impact assessment covers: (a) intended purpose and benefits; (b) foreseeable risks and discrimination risk; (c) data inputs and quality; (d) mitigation measures; (e) post-deployment monitoring plan
Algorithmic discrimination risk specifically addressed in risk profile — analysis of whether system could produce disparate impacts in the covered consequential decision domain
Impact assessment records retained and available for Colorado AG review on request
ID-05.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702(2)(b) — Impact assessment obligation (equivalent to AKSI risk profiling)

evidence_requirements: Access controls for high-risk AI systems documented — part of the risk management program
Note: Colorado does not specify authentication standards; access control evidence contributes to the broader risk management program required under CRS §6-1-1702(2)(a)
PR-01.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702(2)(a) — Risk management program (access controls implied)

evidence_requirements: Scope enforcement for high-risk AI systems documented — system used only for declared consequential decision purpose
Note: Colorado's prohibition on unauthorized use of consumer data in AI decisions is supported by scope enforcement controls
PR-02.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702 — AI system use limited to declared purpose

evidence_requirements: Tool and component provenance verified — part of impact assessment supply chain documentation
Note: Colorado does not specify provenance standards; provenance evidence contributes to impact assessment documentation
PR-03.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702(2)(b) — Impact assessment (provenance as data quality documentation)

evidence_requirements: Consumer personal data used in consequential decisions protected against unauthorized exposure
Consumer data correction mechanism implemented — process for consumers to identify and correct inaccurate personal data used in AI decisions (CRS §6-1-1702(2)(c)(II))
Data accuracy validation in place for personal data used in high-risk AI systems
Records of consumer data correction requests and resolutions maintained
PR-04.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702(2)(c)(II) — Consumer right to correct personal data

evidence_requirements: Audit logs maintained for consequential AI decisions — sufficient to reconstruct the basis for each decision
Impact assessment records retained — records of pre-deployment assessments and annual reviews
Adverse decision records maintained — basis for each adverse consequential decision documented for potential consumer appeal review
Consumer notice delivery records maintained — evidence that pre-decision and adverse-decision notices were provided
PR-05.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702(2) — Documentation obligations; adverse decision records

evidence_requirements: Material changes to high-risk AI systems documented — configuration change records supporting change-triggered re-assessment obligations
Note: Colorado requires re-assessment on material changes; PR-06 configuration integrity monitoring provides the detection signal
PR-06.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702(2)(b) — Impact assessment (re-assessment on material change implied)

evidence_requirements: Personal data of Colorado consumers in transit encrypted — part of risk management program
Note: Colorado does not specify encryption standards; transport security contributes to overall risk management program
High-risk AI systems tested for robustness and discrimination risk before deployment
Testing results documented as part of impact assessment
Note: Colorado impact assessment must cover foreseeable risks — adversarial input and manipulation testing is part of this
PR-08.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702(2)(b) — Impact assessment (foreseeable risks including adversarial inputs)

evidence_requirements: Post-deployment monitoring implemented for each high-risk AI system — per monitoring plan in impact assessment (CRS §6-1-1702(2)(b))
Monitoring specifically covers algorithmic discrimination indicators — disparate impact metrics, error rate analysis by demographic group where feasible
Anomalous outcomes that could indicate discrimination escalated for human review
Monitoring results used as input to annual review (CRS §6-1-1702(2)(d))
DE-01.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702(2)(b) and §6-1-1702(2)(d) — Post-deployment monitoring and annual review

evidence_requirements: Configuration drift detection for high-risk AI systems — material changes trigger re-assessment obligation
Note: Colorado requires ongoing monitoring; DE-02 drift detection supports the annual review and change-triggered re-assessment requirements
DE-02.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702(2)(d) — Annual review obligation (material change detection supports re-assessment trigger)

evidence_requirements: Compliance deviations from risk management policy tracked and remediated
Developer risk disclosures tracked — 90-day disclosure obligations monitored for receipt and response
Annual review compliance tracked — evidence of timely completion of each annual review
AG audit readiness — compliance deviation records available for Colorado AG examination
Impact assessment and audit log integrity protected — records tamper-evident
Note: Colorado requires records to be available to the AG on request; evidence integrity controls support demonstrating that records have not been altered post-decision
DE-04.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702 — Documentation integrity (implied by enforcement obligations)

evidence_requirements: Automated response procedures for discrimination risk discovery documented

Developer 90-day disclosure workflow: if deployer discovers known or reasonably foreseeable risk of algorithmic discrimination, notification process to the Colorado AG and affected parties documented (CRS §6-1-1702(3)(b) — developer obligation; deployer should have internal notification trigger)

Note: Colorado's 90-day AG notification obligation applies explicitly to developers. Deployers should have a response protocol for when monitoring (DE-01) identifies potential discrimination — internal escalation and, if substantiated, AG notification process.
RS-01.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702(3)(b) — 90-day developer disclosure to AG; deployer internal response

evidence_requirements: Consumer appeal mechanism implemented for adverse consequential AI decisions (CRS §6-1-1702(2)(c)(III))
Adverse-decision notice provided to consumer: basis for decision, opportunity to correct personal data, opportunity to appeal (CRS §6-1-1702(2)(c))
Human review process documented for appeal pathway — AI-adverse decisions reviewed by qualified human on consumer request
Appeal response timeline defined and documented — consumer informed of outcome
Records of consumer appeals and outcomes maintained
RS-02.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702(2)(c)(II)-(III) — Consumer data correction and appeal obligation

evidence_requirements: Evidence of each consequential AI decision preserved — sufficient for AG review and consumer appeal
Developer-disclosed risk evidence retained — records of discrimination risk disclosures received from developers
Incident evidence for potential algorithmic discrimination events preserved — monitoring data, decision logs, and corrective action records
Records retained for minimum 5 years (1825 days) — AG enforcement actions may look back over multi-year periods
Rollback capability for high-risk AI systems documented — ability to suspend or revert if discrimination risk confirmed
Note: Colorado does not specify technical rollback requirements; ability to suspend a discriminatory AI system and revert to prior version or manual process is an implied operational control
RC-01.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702(2)(a) — Risk management program (implied operational controls)

evidence_requirements: Annual review completed for each high-risk AI system — confirms system is not causing algorithmic discrimination (CRS §6-1-1702(2)(d))
Annual review documentation retained — methodology, findings, conclusions, and any remediation actions
Post-adverse-finding review: where annual review identifies potential discrimination, root cause analysis and remediation documented

Note: Colorado's annual review is PROACTIVE (calendar-triggered, not incident-triggered). AKSI RC-02 is framed as post-incident. Colorado overlay adds annual proactive review as distinct evidence requirement.
RC-02.framework_reference: CRS §6-1-1702(2)(d) — Annual review obligation (proactive, not incident-triggered)

reporting_obligations.assessment_type: No mandatory third-party certification. Self-certification supported by documented compliance with a recognized AI risk management framework (ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF) provides affirmative defense. Colorado AG may request documentation on complaint or investigation. AG rulemaking may clarify impact assessment methodology and documentation standards.
reporting_obligations.reporting_entity: Colorado Attorney General (coag.gov/ai/). Developer obligation: disclose known or reasonably foreseeable algorithmic discrimination risks to AG and affected deployers within 90 days of discovery.
reporting_obligations.notes: Colorado AG has exclusive enforcement authority — no private right of action. Civil penalties under Colorado Consumer Protection Act: up to $2,000 per violation, up to $500,000 per course of conduct. 60-day cure period applies (except imminent harm). AG rulemaking ongoing at coag.gov/ai/ — rules may clarify impact assessment methodology, consumer notice format, and documentation standards. Safe harbor: compliance with ISO 42001 or NIST AI RMF provides affirmative defense to algorithmic discrimination claims.

human_oversight_mandates.description: Colorado requires a consumer appeal mechanism for adverse consequential AI decisions (CRS §6-1-1702(2)(c)(III)). This implicitly requires human review capacity for consumer appeals. Pre-decision consumer notice and adverse-decision notice obligations require documented oversight configuration. Annual review obligation requires human assessment of AI system outcomes.
human_oversight_mandates.applies_to: All high-risk AI systems making consequential decisions affecting Colorado consumers in covered domains

ID-03: Impact assessment data + consumer data correction

notes: Colorado SB 24-205 (Consumer Protections for Artificial Intelligence Act) — first comprehensive US state AI governance law. Effective June 30, 2026 (delayed from February 1, 2026 by SB 25B-004, signed August 28, 2025). This overlay layers Colorado-specific evidence and threshold adjustments onto the AKSI v0.6 common-control catalog. Triggered by DC-PII, DC-AI, DC-PHI, DC-FIN — covering the primary domains where AI systems make consequential decisions affecting Colorado consumers. Key AKSI evidence gaps addressed by this overlay: (1) GOV-04 consumer notice obligation — evidence requirements add consumer notice delivery records; (2) RC-02 annual proactive review — threshold adjustment adds annual_review_required:true and review_interval_days:365; (3) RS-01 90-day AG notification — threshold adjustment adds discrimination_risk_notification_days:90. Safe harbor: organizations running AKSI with iso-42001 or nist-ai-rmf overlays active are building toward Colorado's affirmative defense. v0.2 planned: incorporate AG rulemaking guidance on impact assessment methodology once published; clarify small business exemption thresholds.
